title: Week 37
subtitle: Early term. If labor starts now, the baby is unlikely to need the NICU.

baby.size: About the size of a bunch of Swiss chard
baby.development: The baby is considered early term. The lungs are close to mature. The grasp is firm and the baby is practicing breathing, sucking, and swallowing in preparation for feeding.

you.body: Your uterus is about six and a half inches above your belly button. You may feel the baby drop, which eases breathing and increases pressure on the bladder. You may have more Braxton Hicks.
you.mind: Early term is a strange place — technically full term, but most babies come later. Try not to read the date as a deadline.

coreActions.title: Ask about a membrane sweep
coreActions.why: It is an option from 39 weeks that can start labor without medication. It is not for everyone, and it is worth knowing it exists before it is offered.
coreActions.detail: A membrane sweep is a physical separation of the membranes from the cervix during a vaginal exam. It can start labor and it can also cause cramping and spotting. It is offered from 39 weeks at most practices. You can decline it. Ask your OB what they recommend and why.

options.label: Ask at your next visit
options.detail: One question. They will bring it up anyway.

options.label: Read about induction options
options.detail: So the conversation is not the first time.

coreActions.skipIf: You are having a planned cesarean, or you have already discussed it.

coreActions.title: Know the difference between early labor and the real thing
coreActions.why: Most people go to the hospital too early the first time. Knowing what early labor feels like saves a trip home.
coreActions.detail: Early labor is contractions that are irregular, mild, and far apart, and they often stop when you rest or change position. Active labor is regular, stronger, and closer together, and it does not stop. If your water breaks, call regardless of contractions.

options.label: Ask your OB for their rule
options.detail: Theirs is the one that counts.

coreActions.title: Rest more than feels necessary
coreActions.why: Labor takes energy, and the first week at home takes more. Rest now is not wasted time — it is the reserve you will draw on.
coreActions.detail: Lie down in the afternoon even if you do not sleep. Say no to one thing this week. Let the house be imperfect. If you are working, take the leave when you can rather than pushing to 39 weeks out of guilt.

options.label: Say no to one thing
options.detail: One social plan, one favor. It counts.

coreActions.skipIf: You are already resting when you can.

personas.headline: You are on call now
personas.body: From 37 weeks the answer to "is this it?" can be yes. Know the route, the bag, and who is driving.

actions.title: Put the bag in the car
actions.why: The bag by the door is a plan. The bag in the car is a decision already made.

actions.title: Save the triage number
actions.why: It is on the fridge in this week's pack. Put it in your phone too, because you will be the one dialling.

personas.headline: The phone stays on
personas.body: The call may come at three in the morning. That is the whole job this month.

actions.title: Keep the phone on at night
actions.why: A silenced phone at 3am is a missed birth. Turn the ringer on and put it by the bed.

actions.title: Cook one meal they can reheat
actions.why: Not a feast. One thing, in portions, that goes in the oven from frozen.

alsoKnow.title: Early term is not the same as full term
alsoKnow.body: 37 to 38 weeks is early term. Babies born then do well, but the last weeks still add brain and lung development. That is why induction is usually not offered before 39 unless there is a reason.

alsoKnow.title: If your water breaks, call
alsoKnow.body: It may be a gush or a slow leak. Note the time and the color. Call your OB even if contractions have not started.

alsoKnow.title: Nesting energy is not a sign of labor
alsoKnow.body: It is common and it is not predictive. Do not lift heavy things or stand on chairs. Let someone else do the high shelves.

redFlags.text: Fluid that keeps leaking, or any vaginal bleeding
A clear change in your baby's usual movement
A severe headache that will not go, or blurred vision or spots

appointments.label: Weekly prenatal visit
appointments.note: Every week. Ask about position and the plan for 39.

sources.title: How to Tell When Labor Begins
